reconstruction: Model: the scooter travels 2 m uphill. Choose the scooter as the system. Motor, friction, gravity and the normal force all belong in the work ledger.
Motor work: +15 N × 2 m = +30 J. Friction work: −3 N × 2 m = −6 J.
Gravity work: −mgh = −3 kg × 10 m/s² × 0.5 m = −15 J. The normal is perpendicular to the trip, so its work is 0 J.
Add every row: net work = 30 − 6 − 15 + 0 = +9 J. It starts at rest, so the final kinetic energy is 9 J.
From ½mv² = 9 J, v² = 2×9/3 = 6 m²/s², so speed at the top is √6 ≈ 2.45 m/s. Positive net work is consistent with reaching the top and gaining speed.
criteria: Did you include all four force contributions, with signs tied to the direction of travel?
Did you add total work before using the kinetic-energy equation?
Did your explanation show why the normal does no work, even though it has a force?
boundary: With motor force 10 N, its work would be +20 J across the full 2 m.
Friction would still contribute −6 J, gravity −15 J and normal 0 J; the would-be net change is −1 J.
Starting from rest, it cannot reach the top unaided because the motion would need negative kinetic energy. It would need additional energy or a stronger push.

reconstruction: Draw two regions. During spring contact the ground is smooth. At the spring's natural length the 2 kg cart is no longer touching the unattached spring.
At the start the spring stores ½kx² = ½ × 200 N/m × (0.10 m)² = 1.00 J.
At release, all 1.00 J is the cart's kinetic energy: ½ × 2 kg × v² = 1.00 J, so v = 1.00 m/s.
Only after release does friction act. On the 0.50 m rough strip, friction work is −1 N × 0.50 m = −0.50 J.
Kinetic energy at the strip's end is 1.00 − 0.50 = 0.50 J. Thus ½ × 2 × v² = 0.50 J, giving v = √0.50 ≈ 0.707 m/s. The cart crosses the strip.
criteria: Did you draw a clear boundary where spring contact ends and the rough strip begins?
Did you use stored spring energy only during contact, and friction work only on the rough section?
Did you carry kinetic energy from the end of region one into region two?
boundary: For a 1.00 m rough strip, friction would use 1 N × 1.00 m = 1.00 J, exactly all the release kinetic energy.
The cart reaches the far end only with zero speed: it has no kinetic energy left there.
It cannot cross a longer rough strip without extra energy. Zero kinetic energy at a turning/stopping point is allowed; negative kinetic energy is not.
